newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Africa Israel managing director quits.
newsitem.headline: Africa Israel managing director quits.

text.p: The managing director of property development firm Africa Israel, Avigdor Kaplan, has resigned after three months on the job because of a conflict between his role and the board chairman's, the developer said on Thursday.
A company statement included a letter from Kaplan in which he attributed his decision to the hands-on approach of board chairman Lev Leviev.
"I found that your serving as an active chairman...does not leave me the space needed in my opinion to fulfil my duties as managing director," Kaplan said in the letter addressed to Leviev.
Israeli media said there were differences of opinion between the two men over various matters, including Leviev's plans to close a Tel Aviv shopping mall on the Jewish Sabbath.
Since Leviev bought a controlling stake in Africa Israel last November and started to bring its policy in line with Orthodox beliefs, several senior managers have left.

Among the company's leading projects is a shopping centre under construction in an upscale secular neighbourhood of Tel Aviv. Leviev, a religious Jew, announced plans to shut the mall every Friday evening until sundown on Saturday in observance of the Sabbath.

The decision fuelled the debate in Israel between those who observe ritual Jewish law and the majority of Israelis who do not. It also raised concern among investors that Africa Israel's profits would suffer.
Leviev, who made much of his fortune in the diamond business, will serve as acting managing director until a replacement for Kaplan is appointed.
The company also has interests in hotels, tourism, industry and trade.
